references.text: The parallel account in Mark about the man who cast out demons in Jesus' name without following the disciples, where Jesus gives the same answer: "Do not stop him".

Jesus states the opposite principle: "Whoever is not with me is against me". Together with Luke 9:50, this shows two sides of the same truth – in relation to Jesus himself, neutrality is impossible, but in relation to how disciples judge other believers, they should show generosity.
Luke's own rendering of Jesus' words "Whoever is not with me is against me", which complements the statement in 9:50 by showing the other side of the principle.

Moses' response when Joshua wanted to stop Eldad and Medad from prophesying in the camp: "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the Lord's people were prophets!" An Old Testament parallel to Jesus' attitude about not stopping those who work in God's power outside the immediate circle.
Paul emphasizes that no one can say "Jesus is Lord" except by the Holy Spirit, which supports the principle that whoever acts in Jesus' name should not be stopped.
Paul rejoices that Christ is preached, even by those who do so with impure motives. This reflects the same principle: what is done in Christ's name should not be hindered.
